subject: Aurora platform: intermittent streaming blackouts and chunked-timeout spikes
messages:
From: Liam Turner <liam@aurora.ai>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@aurora.ai
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Realtime: client-visible stream blackouts (high error-rate)

Hi Soojin,

We started seeing severe intermittent blackouts in our realtime inference streams this morning. Approximately every 10–20 minutes, the WebSocket stream stalls for ~6–20s, then resumes. During those stalls, clients observe chunked-transfer timeouts and a flurry of 502/504 errors. Error rate spiked from our baseline 0.3% to ~6% for the last 4 hours.

We attached a small sample of request IDs and a p95 latency snapshot. Can your team advise whether this is a networking intermediary issue or something on Redwood’s serving layer? This is impacting our live features for enterprise customers.

We are on Dedicated cluster: aurora-prod-us-1, model pinned to rwd-llama-7b-v2-quant.

Attaching: aurora-logs-20270529.zip

Thanks,
Liam Turner
Platform Reliability Lead, Aurora AI

(Attachment: aurora-logs-20270529.zip)

Hi Liam — thanks for the quick report and logs. I’m escalating this immediately to SRE and runtime engineering (cc’d).

Quick notes:
- We’ve kicked off a preliminary correlation against our ingress gateway logs and the Dedicated pool metrics. Initial signals show concurrent increases in chunk-retransmit counters and a short-lived spike in request queue latency in the aurora-prod-us-1 pool around the same timestamps.
- Can you confirm whether you’re using any client-side timeout/backoff config that might magnify the observed 502s?

We’ll follow up within the hour with a triage summary and a mitigation plan. Apologies for the customer impact — we’ll prioritize.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime: client-visible stream blackouts (high error-rate)

Quick triage notes (from runtime):

- Reproduced a similar waveform in our test harness against a pinned rwd-llama-7b-v2-quant variant with the same request shape. Under medium concurrency (20–30 sessions/sec) we saw periodic stalls where the worker’s token emission paused for ~8–12s before resuming.
- The stall correlates with short GC pauses in the VM hosting the model runtime when the KV cache pressure kicked above threshold. It looks like the combination of large prefix caching + quant ops leads to intermittent CPU/GPU synchronization delays.
- No evidence yet of upstream proxy network drops; connection remains established across stalls (i.e., WebSocket stays open but frames are not emitted).

Immediate mitigation I can push: reduce KV cache retention on aurora-prod-us-1 for rwd-llama-7b-v2-quant to remove the GC pressure window, and temporarily lower concurrency cap for Aurora to 15 sessions/sec. That should reduce stall frequency while we implement a more robust async flush.

I’m attaching a p95 latency chart from the test run.

—Dev
(Attachment: p95_latency_chart.png)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: dev_patel@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime: client-visible stream blackouts (high error-rate)

Thanks Dev — good reproduction. Two asks:

1) Dev, please push the KV retention change and the temporary concurrency cap now (we should do this as a flavored config change so we can rollback quickly). Confirm when done so I can monitor.
2) Soojin, this will require an executive sync with Rishi — Aurora is an enterprise customer on a reserved Dedicated contract and they’re experiencing customer-visible outages during peak hours. I recommend we prep a short summary and request a brief exec touchpoint in our 3pm PT slot to avoid escalation to Aurora leadership.

I’ll open a hotspot monitor and enable additional tracing for token emission and GC events on the cluster. If we still see stalls after the cap, we’ll consider a short fallback to a compatible non-quantized variant to maintain availability.

—Karthik

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Subject: URGENT: Exec sync requested — Aurora realtime blackouts (customer-impacting)

Rishi / Vanessa —

Short summary: Aurora (enterprise Dedicated customer) is seeing intermittent WebSocket streaming stalls leading to chunked-transfer timeouts and a ~6% error rate spike. Runtime has reproduced a stall pattern tied to KV cache pressure and GC-driven sync pauses for the rwd-llama-7b-v2-quant variant.

Immediate actions taken:
- Dev pushed a KV cache retention reduction and set a temporary concurrency cap for Aurora to 15 sessions/sec (now in effect).
- Additional tracing and hotspot metrics enabled on aurora-prod-us-1.

Proposed near-term mitigations (0–4 hrs):
- Keep concurrency cap while we roll out an async KV flush (engineering ETA 6–12 hrs).
- If stalls persist during business hours, fallback to rwd-llama-7b-v2 (non-quant) for stability — we expect a modest latency/cost increase but preserve availability.

Request: please join a 15-minute exec sync at 15:00 PT today to approve the fallback and any customer credits/credits messaging. Aurora is sensitive to downtime; I’d like to present the mitigation plan and proposed customer communication.

For context I’ve included sample logs and the p95 chart.

Thanks,
Soojin
